summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis card (L7) proposing a factorial experiment to test whether prior senolytic/SASP clearance reduces the NAD-boosting effect of a CD38 inhibitor (specifically 78c) compared to CD38i alone. The document is a pre-registered hypothesis at the "propose-assay" stage, with all experimental evidence drawn from published literature and the key factorial experiment (CD38i ± senolysis residual ΔNAD) explicitly marked as UNKNOWN and NOT_RUN. It is TRL 1: a concept with mechanistic literature support but no original experimental data.

content_blocks.title: Core Hypothesis / Claim (L7)
content_blocks.content: After documented senescent-cell / SASP clearance lowers CD38 load, residual tissue ΔNAD from a matched CD38-inhibitor pulse is smaller than ΔNAD from the same CD38i without prior clearance at a matched timepoint. Pre-registered threshold: (ΔNAD_CD38i_alone − ΔNAD_CD38i_post-senolysis) ≥ 20% of ΔNAD_CD38i_alone (or alone wins on a pre-registered superiority test). This is a 'subtract-before-add' hypothesis: clear SASP-driven CD38+ macrophage load first, then pulse the same CD38i lever.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale / Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: CD38 gates age-related NAD decline and NMN degradation. SASP induces CD38-high macrophages that drain tissue NAD. Senescent/SASP ablation lowers CD38 and partially restores NAD. Ecto-CD38 block raises NAD via an NMN-dependent route. 78c-class CD38i improves aged-mouse healthspan as monotherapy (not a ± senolysis residual factorial). Symmetric diminishing returns: once CD38 load is subtracted by senolysis, residual CD38i target shrinks, so post-senolysis ΔNAD_CD38i < CD38i-alone ΔNAD. This is distinct from L5/L6 precursor-vs-CD38i ranking.

content_blocks.title: Why It Matters / Context
content_blocks.content: Longevity stacks often add CD38i after or with senolytics expecting more NAD. L5/L6 ranked residual CD38i vs precursor on a missing H2H panel and listed symmetric CD38i shrink only as a competing limitation — they did not measure this same-drug ± senolysis factorial. Soft-claims: discussion — CD38i residual shrink after subtract remains UNKNOWN (78c∩named senolytics soft-complete 0).

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Evidence
content_blocks.content:
Four key published studies cited as mechanistic support:
1. PMID 27304511 (Camacho-Pereira 2016, Cell Metab, DOI 10.1016/j.cmet.2016.05.006, PMC4911708): Age-related NAD decline requires CD38; CD38 is the major in vivo NMN-degrading activity. Status: LITERATURE (confirmed).
2. PMID 33199924 (Covarrubias 2020, Nat Metab, DOI 10.1038/s42255-020-00305-3, PMC7908681): SASP induces CD38-high macrophages that reduce tissue NAD. Status: LITERATURE (confirmed).
3. PMID 33199925 (Chini 2020, Nat Metab, DOI 10.1038/s42255-020-00298-z, PMC8752031): Senescent/SASP ablation ↓CD38 and partially restores NAD; ecto-CD38 block raises NAD NMN-dependently. Status: LITERATURE (confirmed).
4. PMID 35263032 (Tarragó 2022, Aging Cell, DOI 10.1111/acel.13589, PMC9009115): CD38i 78c improves median survival/healthspan in aged mice as monotherapy — not a ± senolysis residual ΔNAD factorial. Status: LITERATURE (confirmed, monotherapy only).

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claimed vs. Baseline Measured
content_blocks.content:
Baseline claimed (by others): After senolysis, CD38i still delivers full monotherapy-class ΔNAD (or stacking CD38i with/after senolytics always adds NAD), so same-drug residual shrink need not be tested; L5/L6 already settled it.

Baseline measured (actual evidence status):
- CD38 gates age NAD / NMN fate: LITERATURE (PMID 27304511)
- SASP→CD38+ macrophages→tissue NAD↓: LITERATURE (PMID 33199924)
- Clearance ↓CD38 + partial NAD rebound; ecto-block NMN-dependent: LITERATURE (PMID 33199925)
- 78c aged-mouse benefit: LITERATURE monotherapy (PMID 35263032)
- Same CD38i ± senolysis residual ΔNAD factorial: UNKNOWN (78c∩named senolytics soft-complete 0; adjacent hits reviews/OA non-match)
- Shrink margin ≥20% of alone-arm Δ: PREDICTION
- L5/L6 do not already prove this — symmetric shrink was limitation only, not a measured claim.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat L5/L6 as proving L7 — they left residual ranking UNKNOWN and listed symmetric CD38i shrink only as a competing limitation.
2. Incomplete clearance: residual CD38+ macrophages can preserve CD38i ΔNAD — shrink is not automatic from 'CD38 fell.'
3. Baseline NAD rebound after clearance can shrink absolute ΔNAD even if fractional CD38i efficacy holds — assay must pre-register residual vs absolute Δ definition; 78c monotherapy ≠ post-subtract residual.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Method and Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content:
Method: propose-assay (NOT_RUN).

Proposed assay design: Aged tissue (WAT/liver) or SASP-conditioned system; vehicle vs senolytic/SASP run-in → matched CD38i pulse at matched timepoint. Measure tissue NAD + CD38 activity. Pre-register residual vs absolute ΔNAD definition, α, and N before running.

Refute if: On the pre-registered ± senolysis panel, residual CD38i ΔNAD after clearance is NOT smaller than CD38i alone by the ≥20% alone-arm margin (or alone fails superiority) when CD38↓ is verified — especially under incomplete clearance where residual CD38+ load remains high, or when shrink is only an absolute-baseline artifact.

Ablation logic:
- Remove ± senolysis run-in factorial with matched CD38i pulse: monotherapy 78c LITERATURE cannot show CD38i ΔNAD shrinks after subtract.
- Remove documented clearance run-in with CD38↓/partial NAD rebound verification: card collapses into generic CD38i dosing comparison.
- Remove L5/L6≠proof + incomplete-clearance + absolute-vs-residual assay discipline: would invent a factorial result left UNKNOWN.

key_findings: This is a TRL 1 hypothesis card: the core factorial experiment (CD38i ± senolysis residual ΔNAD) is explicitly UNKNOWN and NOT_RUN — no original experimental data exists.
The hypothesis proposes that prior senolytic/SASP clearance reduces the NAD-boosting effect of CD38 inhibitor 78c by ≥20% of the alone-arm ΔNAD (pre-registered threshold).

All mechanistic support is from published literature: CD38 gates age NAD decline (PMID 27304511), SASP induces CD38-high macrophages draining tissue NAD (PMID 33199924), senolysis reduces CD38 and partially restores NAD (PMID 33199925), and 78c improves aged-mouse healthspan as monotherapy (PMID 35263032).
The 78c monotherapy aged-mouse data (~10% median survival increase) does NOT constitute evidence for the ± senolysis residual factorial — this is explicitly flagged.
L5/L6 prior cards listed symmetric CD38i shrink only as a competing limitation, not a measured result — they do not prove L7.
Key confounders identified: incomplete clearance (residual CD38+ macrophages), absolute vs. fractional ΔNAD definition, and baseline NAD rebound artifacts.
FTO status is UNKNOWN; ip_class is 'subtract-before-add'; estimated time to refute is 6 weeks at kill_cost_tier=2.
Proposed assay: aged tissue (WAT/liver) or SASP-conditioned system; vehicle vs senolytic/SASP run-in → matched CD38i pulse; measure tissue NAD + CD38 activity with pre-registered α and N.
